text: Over half of large medium-voltage transformers imported came from Mexico in 2024, and imports from South Korea and Colombia grew significantly. China represented approximately 5% of imports in 2024, possibly as a result of Section 301 tariffs significantly increasing the cost of those imports. The most critical and potentially constrained inputs to transformer manufacturing include grain-oriented electric steel (GOES) and continuously transposed conductor copper wire, both of which have limited production capacities in the United States, but which are produced in large quantities in several countries, including China and Russia. Foreign transformer manufacturers can purchase foreign GOES at a lower price than U.S. transformer manufacturers can—because of U.S. tariffs on imported steel—and then manufacture their products abroad and sell their transformers into the United States. There are a variety of other electrical components within a PV system, particularly for large- scale applications, such as high-voltage transformers, combiner boxes, switchgear, circuit breakers, substation components, and transmission-related equipment. Many come from various domestic and international manufacturing locations, including Mexico, Canada, and China. Because of recent increases in U.S. deployment of PV, wind turbines, and electric vehicles— which rely on many of these components—companies have made recent investments to expand domestic manufacturing. Battery Energy Storage Systems Most batteries manufactured globally, including in the United States, are used in electric vehicles. However, stationary storage has become a growing source of demand, representing approximately 14% of global—and 22% of domestic—battery demand in 2024. Domestic utility- scale BESS energy storage capacity grew by 66% in 2024, and 28% of residential PV systems installed in 2024 were paired with BESS. Utility-scale BESS manufacturing capacity in the United States was about 61 GWh at the end of 2024. For comparison, 22 GWh of BESS were imported into the United States in 2024, mainly from China. Companies headquartered in the United States own over half of U.S. utility-scale BESS manufacturing capacity, and over 25% is owned by Chinese-headquartered companies.2 2 The location of a company’s headquarters is where its executives work and key decisions are made; however, the company may have manufacturing, sales, and other operations in other countries. xii This report is available at no cost from the National Laboratory of the Rockies (NLR) at www.nlr.gov/publications. Residential BESS pack manufacturing also continues to scale, with more than 5 GWh of manufacturing capacity added at the end of 2024, largely from Tesla. While non-BESS U.S. battery cell production in 2024 was about 109 GWh, domestic BESS cell production was insignificant.3 Multiple companies started cell production in the first half of 2025. Approximately 10.6 GWh of anode and 9.1 GWh of cathode manufacturing capacity existed in the United States in 2024, all of which came online after 2022.4 An additional 22.0 GWh of anode and of 13.6 GWh of cathode manufacturing capacity was under construction at the end of 2024.
